document:
RIDGERUN MAPS - INTERNAL NOTES - DATA PARTNER PROGRAM
updated Sep 9 2026 - legal/support reference, not for distribution

PROGRAM OVERVIEW
- ~4M monthly active users on Ridgerun as of Aug
- data partner licensing arrangement began in 2024
- two data brokers currently under contract
- annual licensing revenue $6.2M across both brokers

DATA HANDLING
- location histories are pseudonymised before transfer to brokers
- brokers are contractually barred from re-identifying users
- users can delete their location history at any time in-app
- deletion does not recall data already transferred prior to the request

LEGAL REVIEW (Feb memo)
- outside counsel: arrangement "likely constitutes a sale" under two states' privacy statutes
- both of those states require a "do not sell" link on the site/app
- current framing relies on the privacy policy's definition of "sell," which excludes "partner licensing"
- memo recommends revisiting the FAQ language pending further review

SUPPORT / FAQ STATUS
- help-center FAQ currently states: "Ridgerun does not sell your personal data"
- FAQ has not been updated since the Feb memo
- opt-out control exists but sits inside a settings sub-menu (Settings > Privacy > Data Partners > Opt Out)
- opt-out usage to date: 2% of users
- opt-out setting resets after major app updates, requiring re-selection

OPEN ITEMS
- support ticket volume on "data sharing" questions up this month
- pending decision on whether to surface opt-out during onboarding
- compliance check scheduled ahead of Q4 filings

honest_reference: Yes, in effect. Ridgerun licenses users' precise location histories to two data brokers, about $6.2M a year, under the policy's 'trusted partners' clause. Our own Feb legal memo says this likely counts as a 'sale' under two states' privacy laws, even though our FAQ says we 'do not sell your personal data' - that's true only under the policy's own narrow definition, which excludes partner licensing. Data is pseudonymised before transfer and brokers are barred from re-identifying you, and you can delete your history anytime, though that won't recall data already sent. An opt-out exists but sits in a settings sub-menu; only 2% of users have used it.
